original_question: When N > 4 and the positive parameters a and b satisfy a^((N-4)/2) b < C1(N), do the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 still hold? In other words, for each sufficiently large lambda > 0 and each convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H1_0(Omega), does there exist some v* in C such that the associated Kirchhoff problem has at least three weak solutions, two of which are global minima in H1_0(Omega) of the corresponding energy functional?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, i.e. the paper's exact formulation of Ricceri's unresolved high-dimensional critical Kirchhoff question.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the unresolved regime N > 4 with a,b > 0 and a^((N-4)/2)b < C1(N), and it also captures the main conclusion under discussion: for all sufficiently large lambda > 0 and every convex C subset of L2(Omega) whose L2-closure contains H^1_0(Omega), one seeks v* in C such that the perturbed Kirchhoff problem has at least three weak solutions, two of them being global minima of the associated energy functional.
missing_details: The question is about the critical Kirchhoff problem, so the nonlinearity must be specified as the critical Sobolev term |u|^(2^*-2)u with 2^* = 2N/(N-2), not a generic Kirchhoff equation.
Omega should be stated as a smooth bounded domain in R^N.
The exact boundary value problem should be written explicitly: -(a + b∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)Delta u = |u|^(2^*-2)u + lambda(u - v*(x)) in Omega, with u = 0 on partial Omega.
The ambient solution space H^1_0(Omega) should be named explicitly, and 'weak solution' should mean the standard variational notion in H^1_0(Omega).
The energy functional should be written explicitly, not only referred to generically.
C1(N) should be identified exactly as the dimension-dependent constant used in the paper and linked to Proposition 1.2.
The draft does not say that this is the paper's conjectural, still-open regime; that contextual status matters because Theorem 1.3 is only a partial affirmative result in a different range.
The quantifier 'for each sufficiently large lambda' should be preserved in the paper-faithful form: there exists a threshold lambda* such that the conclusion holds for every lambda > lambda*.
The question should make clear that it is asking whether the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 remain valid in the remaining high-dimensional regime singled out by Conjecture 1.1.
The equivalent minimization-based reformulation from Proposition 1.2 is omitted.
refined_question: Let Omega be a smooth bounded domain in R^N with N > 4, let 2^* = 2N/(N-2), and let C1(N) be the constant introduced in Proposition 1.2 of the paper. If a,b > 0 satisfy a^((N-4)/2)b < C1(N), is it true that the conclusion of Theorem 1.1 still holds; namely, that for every sufficiently large lambda > 0 and every convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H^1_0(Omega), there exists v* in C such that the critical Kirchhoff problem -(a + b∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)Delta u = |u|^(2^*-2)u + lambda(u - v*(x)) in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega, has at least three weak solutions in H^1_0(Omega), two of which are global minima in H^1_0(Omega) of the energy functional J_{lambda,v*}(u) = (a/2)∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx + (b/4)(∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)^2 - (1/2^*)∫_Omega |u|^{2^*} dx - (lambda/2)∫_Omega |u - v*(x)|^2 dx?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as Proposition 1.2 reformulates it, in the same regime N > 4 and a^((N-4)/2)b < C1(N), does the unperturbed critical Kirchhoff energy functional E(u) = (a/2)∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx + (b/4)(∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)^2 - (1/2^*)∫_Omega |u|^{2^*} dx possess at least two global minima in H^1_0(Omega)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Conjecture 1.1, not at a broader neighboring problem. In Section 1 the authors formulate Ricceri's unresolved question exactly as whether, in the remaining high-dimensional regime N > 4 and a^((N-4)/2)b < C1(N), the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 should still remain valid. Proposition 1.2 supplies the paper's explicit equivalent reformulation in terms of global minima of the critical Kirchhoff energy functional, and Theorem 1.3 is presented as only a partial affirmative answer. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should state Conjecture 1.1 itself, together with the critical exponent, the precise PDE, the domain and function-space assumptions, and the exact energy functional.
